Vendored browser libraries for the WTF consumer site.

WHY VENDORED, NOT CDN-LOADED
This is a Canadian civic-transparency site. Loading libraries from unpkg or
jsdelivr announces every reader's browser to a third party on every page view,
which is at odds with the platform's local-sovereign principle, and it makes
the map's availability depend on someone else's uptime. These are served from
our own origin instead.

The previous /map additionally pulled raster basemap TILES from
basemaps.cartocdn.com — a request per tile, per pan, per reader. Those are gone
entirely: the province geometry in /static/canada-provinces.geojson IS the
geography this site draws.

FILES (all UMD builds, loaded in this order — d3-geo depends on d3-array,
which depends on internmap)
  internmap.min.js    internmap@2.0.3
  d3-array.min.js     d3-array@3.2.4
  d3-geo.min.js       d3-geo@3.1.1

60 KB total, replacing ~145 KB of Leaflet plus its stylesheet plus tiles.

TO UPDATE
  npm install d3-geo@<version>
  cp node_modules/{internmap,d3-array,d3-geo}/dist/*.min.js consumer/static/vendor/
  update the versions above, then re-run tests/test_wtf_map.py

DATA (not a library) — consumer/static/world-countries.geojson
  Natural Earth 1:110m Admin 0 Countries (public domain, naturalearthdata.com).
  Reduced to {properties:{code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), name}}; 177 features,
  2 carry no code (N. Cyprus, Somaliland) and are drawn as no-data.
  Boundaries are Natural Earth's de facto lines and are not an endorsement of any
  claim. Used only by the "world" scope of wtf-map.js; loaded on first use.
